cases.question: Which button swings the sword?
cases.answer: The A button swings the sword.

cases.question: How much does the Blue Candle cost?
cases.answer: The Blue Candle costs 60 rupees. It can be purchased for 60 Rupees from a shop reached through a door one screen west of a specific spot in the overworld, and a 2nd Quest hidden shop also sells it for 60 rupees.

cases.question: How many Heart Containers do I need to get the White Sword?
cases.answer: You need five Heart Containers to receive the White Sword, according to the Items and Hyrule 3 documents. One Quest 1 overworld entry says six heart containers are needed for the White Sword in a cave near a river, which is a discrepancy in the sources.

cases.question: Which item can I find in Level-3 of the first quest?
cases.answer: In Level 3 of the first quest, you can find the Raft (the walkthrough says that going down the stairwell in the compass room area leads to the Raft) and a Heart Container and the third Triforce piece are listed as objectives. Specifically, the Raft is found down the stairs from the room reached after the Compass room.

cases.question: How powerful is the Magic Sword?
cases.answer: The Magic Sword has Damage 4, making it the most powerful sword in the game and four times as powerful as the wooden sword.

cases.question: How can I sail across the sea?
cases.answer: Use the Raft, which allows Link to cross lakes and oceans, but it can only be used at a Dock; neither of the 'double docks' triggers raft use.

cases.question: Is there somewhere my hearts get refilled without paying?
cases.answer: Yes. Fairies fill Link's hearts: a fairy dropped by enemies fills 3 hearts, and in the fairy ponds the fairy fills all of your heart meters.

cases.question: How can I win cash by gambling?
cases.answer: The documents mention a Money Making Game, which is the closest thing to gambling for cash. In Hyrule 1 you walk inside the tree in section D-2, and in Hyrule 6 you bomb the middle of the north wall in C-5 to reach a cave with it. In Hyrule 2 you bomb the cliff wall just left of center in A-5 to find the cave. The documents do not explain how the game works or how to win in it.

cases.question: What can I buy at D-4 in section 2 of the overworld?
cases.answer: At D-4 in Hyrule section 2 (2nd Quest), you can buy the ability to use Arrows for 80 rupees, the Magical Shield for 130 rupees, and a set of 4 Bombs for 20 rupees.

cases.question: What happens if I register my name as ZELDA?
cases.answer: Entering your name as "Zelda" at the start of the game immediately begins the Second Quest without playing the First Quest. The documents do not explicitly state whether the name is case-sensitive, so it is not confirmed that "ZELDA" in all capitals triggers the same effect.

cases.question: Where can I buy the Blue Candle, and what can it be used for?
cases.answer: You can buy the Blue Candle for 60 Rupees in a door found from the Fairy Fountain route in Quest 1: from the Fairy Fountain, go three screens south, two screens west, collect the 30 Rupees, return to heal, then go two screens south, four screens east, collect the other 30 Rupees, go one screen west and enter the door. It throws a flame a short distance, can light dark dungeon rooms, burn bushes in the overworld, and damage enemies, but can only be used once per screen.

cases.question: Who is the boss of Level-1 in the first quest and how do I defeat him?
cases.answer: The boss of Level 1 in the first quest is Aquamentus. Strike him in the head six times with the Wooden Sword or three times with the White Sword, timing strikes between the energy orbs he emits from his horn. Only the Magical Shield absorbs the orbs, and sword beams can hit any part of his body.

cases.question: What do I need to enter Level-4 in the first quest, and which item is inside?
cases.answer: You need the Raft, per the Dungeon 4 prerequisites. The documents don't say which single item is inside the entrance. The dungeon's objectives list the Ladder, a Heart Container, and the fourth Triforce piece as things to obtain there.

cases.question: How do I beat the dragon boss?
cases.answer: The dragon boss Aquamentus has 6 HP and shoots fireballs that split in three directions; it can only be blocked by the Magical Shield. It is vulnerable to the Sword and Arrows, and can also be killed by two Bombs. Gleeok, another dragon, requires destroying every attached head.

cases.question: How do I defeat Gleeok?
cases.answer: The only way to defeat a Gleeok is to stab each of its attached heads until they fly free, then destroy every one of the freed heads; the number of heads varies by dungeon (two, three, or four). Defeating it earns a Heart Container.

cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: In the second quest, which dungeon has the Ladder?
cases.answer: The documents do not state which dungeon contains the Ladder in the second quest. Dungeon 6 of Quest 2 lists obtaining the Ladder as an objective, and Dungeon 7 requires collecting the Ladder before entering, so the Ladder appears to be obtained in Dungeon 6 of the second quest, though the documents do not explicitly say it is located there.

cases.question: How can I attack?
cases.answer: Swing the sword with the A button. You can also use a subweapon with the B button, such as the Magical Rod, which fires magical blasts.

cases.question: Which button do i have to press to attack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword, which is how you attack. The B button is used for subweapons.

cases.question: How can I atack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing your sword. Press the B button to use your equipped subweapon, such as the Magical Wand, which fires blasts even without full life.

cases.question: how do i open the menu
cases.answer: Press the Start button on the NES controller to bring up the sub-screen menu, where Link can look at the map, change subweapon, and more. Press Start again to return from the sub-screen to the normal view.

cases.question: can i blow up walls with bombz?
cases.answer: Yes, bombs can blast holes in weak walls. The item description says bombs are used to kill enemies or blast holes in weak walls, and the walkthroughs mention bombing walls to reveal hidden passages.

cases.question: how do i use my secondary item
cases.answer: Press the B button to use your subweapon. Only one item in the blue box can be assigned to B, and you can change that assignment by switching to the sub-screen with Start.

cases.question: how do i atack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword. You can also press B to use your selected subweapon.

cases.question: how can i heal?
cases.answer: You can heal by going to the Fairy Fountain, where the fairy fills all your heart meters, or by drinking a Water of Life, which completely refills your life bar. A Fairy enemy drop fills 3 hearts. Medicine women in caves can sell you a Red Potion for 68 Rupees or a Water of Life for 40 Rupees if you've shown them the Letter.

cases.question: where do i find money?
cases.answer: Several places in the game have money. The Money Making Game is in a cave bombed into the rock face immediately left of the start screen (cheats). Other options include a Money Making Game inside a tree in Hyrule 1 section D-2 (2nd Quest), a 30 Rupee secret cave in Hyrule 1 B-3 (2nd Quest), a 30 Rupee Red Moblin cave at Hyrule 8 B-4 (1st Quest), and a 10 Rupee stairwell under a burned tree at Hyrule 8 B-2 (2nd Quest).

cases.question: what is the best weapon?
cases.answer: The most powerful sword in the game is the Magic Sword, which deals 4 damage and is four times as powerful as the Wooden Sword. Link must have twelve Heart Containers before he can receive it.

cases.question: how do i open a locked door?
cases.answer: One documented method is a cheat: when you enter the first dungeon, immediately leave and come back, and the locked door will open. Otherwise, keys open locked doors, with each key opening one door, and you can carry up to nine until you obtain the magic key.

cases.question: what do i do if ig im stuck
cases.answer: The documents suggest that if you're unsure how to proceed through a dungeon, bomb every wall that does not contain a door, since you will typically find passageways leading further in. It is also not uncommon to find passages to rooms in the "eyes" or unmarked rooms on the dungeon map.

cases.question: how do i defeat the dragon?
cases.answer: The dragon is Gleeok, a multi-headed dragon boss. Link must attack each head, and when a head takes enough damage it detaches and flies around the room; the flying heads cannot be hit, so dodge their projectiles and keep attacking the attached heads until every head is disconnected.

cases.question: where do i get bombs?
cases.answer: In Quest 1, you get bombs by defeating the Moblins in the nearby area until they drop Bombs you can collect (zelda1:overworld-quest-1:002). In Quest 2, a checklist item says to get some Bombs early on, without specifying where (zelda1:overworld-quest-2:001). In the Quest 1 Dungeon 6 resupply, replacement Bombs are obtained a few screens away from the Water of Life woman (zelda1:underworld-quest-1-dungeon-6:004).

cases.question: how do i unlock the bow?
cases.answer: In Quest 1, Dungeon 1, the Bow is found in room O-1, a room with Traps in each corner and a stairwell in the center surrounded by blocks. Push the left most block aside to enter the stairwell, where you'll find the Bow. You'll need to purchase Arrows to use it, unless you already bought them before finding the bow.

cases.question: how do i save my game?
cases.answer: To save your game, choose "SAVE" on the Game Over screen using Select and then press Start; all your accomplishments are stored until you next play. You can also quickly reach the Save Screen from the sub-screen menu by pressing Up (D-pad) and A simultaneously on controller 2.

cases.question: how do i get more hearts?
cases.answer: Heart Containers give Link an additional heart permanently, and they can be obtained in several places. Quest 1 notes that a heart container can be found by burning a fourth tree on a Lake Hylia coast screen, and that the sixth Heart Container can be gotten by bombing a huge rock near the eastern mountains. Quest 2 lists pushing a tombstone in the Graveyard to get a Heart Container. Fairies from enemy drops or fairy ponds refill hearts but do not add permanent ones.

cases.question: can i buy a better shield?
cases.answer: Yes. A Magical Shield is sold in shops, for 90 Rupees in the hidden shop found by burning a tree on the Quest 1 overworld (and the seashore/forest route), and also in other shops for 160 or 130 Rupees in the 2nd Quest overworld. The Magical Shield reflects more enemy attacks than the Small Shield you start with.

cases.question: how do i see in dark rooms?
cases.answer: Use a candle to light dark rooms: the Blue Candle can be used once per screen, and the Red Candle has no per-screen limit. Candles can light up dark rooms in dungeons.

cases.question: Which button do I press to jump?
cases.answer: Press the A button to jump in the air. You jump the same height whether you tap or hold it.

cases.question: How many spirit points does the windmill star cost?
cases.answer: The windmill star costs 5 spirit points to throw.

cases.question: How many lives does Ryu start with?
cases.answer: Ryu starts the game with two lives in reserve.

cases.question: What happens if the clock runs out before I finish a stage?
cases.answer: You lose one life if the timer runs out before you complete a stage.

cases.question: How can I get higher using just one wall?
cases.answer: Use the wall hop technique: jump toward a wall and cling to it, hold the jump button, push away from the wall, then immediately push back toward it as you let go, which lets Ryu rise and cling higher than where he started. Repeating this correctly multiple times can take him to the top of the screen.

cases.question: Who attacks me in Stage 2-3?
cases.answer: In Stage 2-3, you are first attacked by the enemy known as Bomberhead, who moves at a slow, menacing pace and has a spinning weapon with better reach than the enemies before it.

cases.question: Who is the boss of Stage 3-3?
cases.answer: The boss of Stage 3-3 (Act III) is Basaquer.

cases.question: What does the fire wheel do and does it use spirit points?
cases.answer: The Fire Wheel surrounds Ryu with a circle of fire that eliminates any enemy that contacts him. It uses no spirit points, but it replaces any weapon you currently hold and disappears after five seconds, leaving you with no secondary weapon.

cases.question: What is Ninja Gaiden called in Europe?
cases.answer: In Europe, Ninja Gaiden is known as Shadow Warriors.

cases.question: how do i atack?
cases.answer: Press the B button to attack by swinging your sword, and squat (press Down on the D-pad while on the ground) and press B to attack low. To use a secondary weapon, hold Up on the D-pad while pressing B, provided you have enough spirit points.

cases.question: how do i get more ninpo?
cases.answer: Ninpo (secondary weapon power) comes from spirit points, which you collect from blue and red tiles liberated from item containers placed throughout each stage. Blue tiles give 5 points and red tiles give 10 points. The documents do not explicitly use the term 'ninpo', so this assumes it refers to spirit points.

cases.answer: The documents mention health-restoring potions you can collect in the stages: a lamp on the left after the bridge in Stage 4-2 gives a potion that restores some health, and a health-restoring potion is found in an insect item in Stage 2-2 and in a lamp/candle in Stage 5-2. Collecting these items is how you heal according to the documents.

cases.question: why did i get sent back to 6-1?
cases.answer: In Stage 6-3, if you lose to any of the final bosses you are returned all the way to 6-1, regardless of how many lives you have left. Defeated bosses stay dead, so the Masked Devil will not have to be faced again after you return.
